solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dig first for peat, a feature of Ireland

indicators.note: asking for the first of a word means keeping only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of peat
a lough is an Irish lake, the local spelling of the Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A turf-cutter is told that the first job in Ireland is digging the peat bogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ireland's loughs, like Lough Neagh, are its lakes; the peat bog in the surface is only scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: To plough land is to turn over the soil, a kind of digging done with a blade drawn across a field.

clue.text: Veg sounding wonderful, but we see nothing in it?

parts.note: a pea is a green vegetable

indicators.note: something sounding like a word is judged by ear, so the spoken form counts and the spelling changes

parts.note: super means wonderful, and a soup-related spelling says it the same way

explanation.surface: Someone praises a vegetable dish and then complains they cannot see anything in the bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: PEA-SOUPER is old London slang for a fog thick and yellow like pea soup; 'it' in the surface seems to be the dish but is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense fog cuts visibility to almost zero, so in such murk people can make out nothing at all.

clue.text: Stupid view? It's more than right

parts.note: obtuse means slow-witted
an angle on a matter is a point of view

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a foolish opinion, arguing it goes beyond merely being correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like correct, but it is the right angle of geometry, ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry an obtuse corner measures between ninety and one hundred and eighty degrees, exceeding a right one.

clue.text: Proceed with angular measure ignoring a sort of knot

parts.note: to proceed is to go

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: the radian is the SI unit of angle
the letter to remove, taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for tying a knot, telling you to measure the angle while skipping one kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The radian is the mathematician's unit of angle, about 57 degrees; 'a sort of knot' hides that the A belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gordian knot of legend was impossibly tangled until Alexander cut it, so the adjective names that particular knot.

clue.text: For heathen, lawyer produces publicity

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a pagan is a heathen
DA is a US District Attorney

explanation.surface: An attorney defending an unbeliever drums up press coverage for the case.
explanation.walkthrough: DA, District Attorney, is the American public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information spread to promote a cause, a slanted form of promotional material.

clue.text: Less polished diamonds accepted by king perhaps for pounds

indicators.note: being accepted in place of another means taking its slot, one letter swapped for another
one thing for another means instead of it, marking what is replaced

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
a king is one example of a ruler
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A monarch takes rough diamonds as payment instead of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In RULER the L, for pounds, makes way for D, for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean rough and unrefined, so the comparative describes something cruder or with fewer refinements.

clue.text: Footmen work over time to get covered by chroniclers

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something over flips it end to end

parts.note: an op is a work, as in opus

indicators.note: something covered by another sits inside it

parts.note: diarists chronicle their days
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Liveried servants put in overtime so that the society diarists will write about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Footmen' suggests servants in livery, but it is a cryptic way of naming foot specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: Podiatrists treat the feet, so they are humorously men of the foot, a crossword-style rereading of a servant's title.

clue.text: Old prime minister that is twice introduced to supreme king

indicators.note: what is introduced to something is put into it

parts.note: grand means supreme, as in grand master
viz is the abbreviation of videlicet, namely or that is
i.e. (id est) is a second way of writing that is
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A former head of government is presented two times to the all-powerful monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is twice' asks for both abbreviations meaning that is, VIZ and IE, which go between GRAND and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The grand vizier was chief minister of the Ottoman sultan, effectively the head of the government in historical times.

clue.text: In drowsy state, daughter gives way to new invalid condition

indicators.note: giving way to another means stepping aside so it takes your place

parts.note: a sleepy, sluggish state is dullness
D is the abbreviation for daughter
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A sleepy daughter makes way for a fresh invalid, as if at a sickbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a sick person, but here it is the adjective meaning void.
explanation.definitionFit: Something null has no legal force, so the state of being null is one of having no validity.

clue.text: Are you one to have problems eating this?

definitions.text: Are you one to have problems eating this?

parts.note: thou art is the old form of you are
I is the Roman numeral one
to choke is to struggle when swallowing

explanation.surface: A host asks a guest whether they find this particular vegetable difficult to get down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole question is both wordplay and definition: the 'choke' of a globe artichoke is the hairy inedible centre that diners must remove.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe vegetable is famously awkward to eat, with tough leaves and a fibrous heart that can make diners gag.

clue.text: Nobel author removing one line further on in the text

indicators.note: taking away one of something leaves the rest without it

parts.note: Saul Bellow won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1976
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A prize-winning novelist cuts a line from a later page of their book.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLOW has two Ls; one of them goes.
explanation.definitionFit: In a document, see below points the reader to something that comes later on the page.

clue.text: Supplier of pub provides empty bar with jug

indicators.note: an emptied word has its insides scooped out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of bar
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: The firm that stocks a pub hands over an empty bar and a pitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' sits naturally beside pub but is just letters to hollow out.
explanation.definitionFit: Breweries make the beer that pubs sell, and many British pubs are tied to one brewing company.

clue.text: Cheek ring, a symbol of independence

parts.note: a liberty is a piece of impudence, as in what a liberty
to give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them, a ring

explanation.surface: A ring worn through the cheek is held up as a badge of freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give us a bell' is British for 'give me a phone call'; cheek means impudence, not the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The cracked bell in Philadelphia is an emblem of American freedom, linked to the Declaration of 1776.

clue.text: Having grown, wood's first to be cut down

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of wood
axed means felled, cut down

explanation.surface: A forester notes that once a tree has matured it is the first to be felled.
explanation.walkthrough: Waxed is the moon's verb: it waxes as it grows and wanes as it shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is an old verb for to increase, still used of the moon swelling towards full.

clue.text: Fuss, having to swap foot-and-mouth activities

definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: what the feet and the mouth do, listed with the mouth's activity put first

explanation.surface: A fuss blows up over a foot-and-mouth outbreak forcing farmers to change their routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Feet dance and mouths sing; swapping the order of 'dance and song' gives the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a big performance about something is an idiom for creating an unnecessary commotion over it.

clue.text: More crazy to drop initial promise — end of story

indicators.note: dropping an initial means losing the opening letter

parts.note: daft is crazy, so dafter is crazier
to give your word is to promise

explanation.surface: Someone still more foolish breaks their promise, and that is the end of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of story' sounds like a curt 'and that's that', but it is literally the part that closes a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterword is a closing section added to a book after the main text has finished.

clue.text: Drop lifeless: for example, a coffin must follow

parts.note: dead means lifeless
A is one example of a letter of the alphabet
box is slang for a coffin

explanation.surface: Someone collapses dead, and the coffin will come next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a verb for falling dead, but it is the spy's noun: a secret place to leave messages.
explanation.definitionFit: In espionage a drop is a hidden location where agents leave items for each other without meeting.

clue.text: Displacing son during excursion

indicators.note: something happening during another falls within it

parts.note: an outing is a trip or excursion
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy is pushed aside on a family day trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The son is the usual one-letter abbreviation, slipped into a word for a day trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to force them out of a position, so it is a synonym for pushing them aside.

clue.text: Golf club admitting West and North African

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the R and A, Royal and Ancient, is the St Andrews club that governs golf
W is the abbreviation for west
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A golf club accepts members from the West and the North of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal and Ancient is written R and A, so its letters are R-AND-A; W goes in after the R and N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rwandan is a person from Rwanda, a nation in east-central Africa, so it names one kind of African.

clue.text: At sea, declare how weather has improved

definitions.note: a phrase describing the verb: the weather has done this

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Out on a ship, a sailor announces that conditions have got better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits the weather picture perfectly but only signals a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: When rain and cloud pass and the sky turns bright, people say the weather has become fine again.

clue.text: OK to develop preparation for each task

parts.note: planning is preparation
per means for each, as in per head
a mission is a task

explanation.surface: A manager signs off on drawing up a plan for every assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, planning permission is the council's consent needed before building on or altering land.
explanation.definitionFit: Local authority approval lets a landowner build, so it is literally an official go-ahead to develop a site.

clue.text: Page unfinished judge takes on to work out

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
an umpire judges a game
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge picks up an incomplete page and tries to make sense of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like solve, but it is exercising in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump iron is an idiom for lifting weights, which is a form of training in a gym.

clue.text: Key mistake admitted by party-pooper

indicators.note: what is admitted by something is let inside it, so the letters sit within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two parts

explanation.surface: A spoilsport owns up to a serious error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like main, but it is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing error, made by hitting the wrong key on a keyboard.

clue.text: Old vegetation river leaves behind

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: when something leaves, it departs and is no longer there

parts.note: verdure is lush green vegetation
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Old plants are left stranded after the river moves away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' tempts as foliage beside vegetation; it is the verb, and 'behind' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind schedule means late, which is what an unpaid bill or late train is.

clue.text: At length, opponents destroyed continent

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for length
antis are those against something

explanation.surface: Eventually, enemies ruined a whole landmass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At length' reads as finally, but it splits into AT and L; 'destroyed' looks like an anagram signal and belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Plato's legend, the island realm sank beneath the ocean in a single day, a lost land.

clue.text: Hard, unresponsive, not feminine

indicators.note: saying not of a letter means it is excluded

parts.note: frigid means cold and unresponsive
F is the abbreviation for feminine

explanation.surface: A description of someone stern and cold, lacking softness.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIGID loses its leading F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rigid is stiff and unbending, a direct synonym for firm or solid.

clue.text: Shabby magistrate read poorly

parts.note: the Doge was chief magistrate of Venice

indicators.note: done poorly means done badly, so the letters end up in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scruffy judge stumbles through his reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The Doge was the elected ruler and chief magistrate of the Venetian republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A book with folded page corners looks worn and tatty, so the word extends to anything well-worn.

clue.text: In quarrel rod snapped off on top of head

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it
a stick snapped off has lost its end

parts.note: a stick is a rod
the dome is the crown of the head

explanation.surface: During a fight, someone breaks a rod over another person's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface violence is a fair picture of a household row; 'top of head' is a whole part of the skull, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: British police and press call a row between partners at home a domestic, a noun use of the adjective.

clue.text: Send for engineers to achieve objective

parts.note: to send for a doctor is to get one
the RE, the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: A commander calls in the engineers so the mission can succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are known as the RE, so the regiment brings its article with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get there is an idiom for finally succeeding, reaching a goal after effort.

clue.text: Clothes hang on one end of line

parts.note: to linger is to hang on, stay longer
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of line

explanation.surface: Garments are pegged out on the end of a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang' and 'line' build a laundry picture; 'hang on' is one verb, to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightwear, a particular category of garments.

clue.text: Appear, since having resolved dangers

parts.note: to emerge is to appear

indicators.note: something resolved has been broken down and worked out afresh, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone comes out of hiding because the threats have been dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved dangers' reads as threats dealt with; 'resolved' acts on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergencies are sudden crises that put people at risk, so they are perils requiring urgent action.

clue.text: Typical — only the second half is quarrelsome

indicators.note: keeping only the back half means throwing away the front half

parts.note: characteristic means typical

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that it is so like them to be argumentative in the second half.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARACTERISTIC has fourteen letters; its last seven give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eristic comes from the Greek for strife and describes argument for its own sake, contentious debate.

clue.text: Sterile land treated and brought back into use

indicators.note: something treated has been processed and altered, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Barren farmland is fertilised and returned to cultivation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like farming; 'treated' is the mixing signal on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment set up again in its place has been restored to service, put back for people to operate.

clue.text: Sponsor keeps changing representative

indicators.note: changing letters means altering their arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A backer keeps replacing the person who speaks for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' reads as a verb but is part of the letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesperson talks officially on behalf of an organisation, acting as its public voice.

clue.text: Interior desperate for nourishment, introduced directly

parts.note: INT is the abbreviation for interior, as in film scripts
ravenous means extremely hungry

explanation.surface: Someone starving at the core is fed straight in, as by a drip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nourishment fits a hospital drip neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: An intravenous drug goes straight into a vein, entering the bloodstream without passing through the gut.

clue.text: Put into new vessel, stuck, having broken shin inside

indicators.note: to have something inside is to hold it
a thing placed inside another is enclosed within it

parts.note: trapped means stuck

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be put together differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient is moved to another vessel, trapped with a fractured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' could be a vein, but it is a ship; the jumbled leg-bone sits inside TRAPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To tranship cargo is to unload it from one ship and load it onto another for onward carriage.

clue.text: Court formality, a warning sign

parts.note: starch is stiffness of manner
amber is the traffic light that warns of a change

explanation.surface: Courtroom ceremony serves as a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain amber is the name for the yellow traffic light; 'court formality' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was an English royal tribunal abolished in 1641, famous for secretive arbitrary judgments.

clue.text: Doing nothing wrong, sample food that's aesthetically pleasing

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is the zero, nothing
to taste food is to sample it

explanation.surface: Behaving correctly, a diner tries a dish that looks lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing nothing wrong' reads as innocence, but splits into word, zero and mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in good taste shows refined judgment and is attractive to a discerning eye.

clue.text: Blend is endless, good for a book

indicators.note: one thing for another means in its place

parts.note: interminable means never-ending
G is the abbreviation for good
A as written and B, the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A reader complains that a mixture of styles makes a novel feel never-ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' looks like a deletion signal, but it is the long word INTERMINABLE, whose AB becomes G.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermingle is to mix things together so they combine, a direct synonym of the definition.

clue.text: It doesn't pay to divert a bus, overall

indicators.note: diverting something sends it a different way, rearranging its route

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A transport manager decides that rerouting a bus is not worth it on balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It doesn't pay' sounds like a verdict on cost, but it describes work with no wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced work done without wages earns the worker nothing, so it literally gives no payment.

clue.text: In short have half of gorge to cross

indicators.note: what is put in something sits inside it

parts.note: terse means short, curt

indicators.note: taking half of a word discards the remaining part

parts.note: a ravine is a gorge

explanation.surface: Briefly, a hiker needs to get across half a canyon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' reads as briefly, but 'short' is a word to hold the first three letters of RAVINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse ground is to travel across it from one side to the other.

clue.text: Deficiency the result of extended summer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an amount by which something is lacking
second meaning, cryptic: if summer runs long, the American autumn that follows is brief

explanation.surface: A drought warning: a prolonged summer leaves supplies running low.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for autumn; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is an amount by which something falls short of what is needed, a lack.

clue.text: Not all were wrong to waste day in garden

parts.note: part means not all

indicators.note: wasting something means losing it, so it drops out

parts.note: erred means were wrong
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Some people were mistaken to spend a whole day idling among the flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: A parterre is the French-style formal garden of grand country houses such as Versailles.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal ornamental garden laid out with flower beds in a geometric pattern.

clue.text: Obstruct seat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold up or delay progress
second meaning: a seat in a theatre's ground floor or a choir

explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the stalls are the seats on the ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to delay something deliberately and a fixed place to sit, as in choir stalls.

clue.text: Modern sort of saint?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to recent times
second meaning: a member of the Mormon church

explanation.walkthrough: Mormons call themselves the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a present-day version of something and also the Mormon name for church members.

clue.text: Being right up close, a knocking of heads

parts.note: taken as written
butting is striking with the head

explanation.surface: Two people stand so near that their heads knock together.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a knocking of heads' as A plus BUTTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Properties that abut share a boundary, touching with no gap between them.

clue.text: Comfortable with trigonometrical expression

definitions.meaning: second meaning: cos y, the cosine of an angle y

explanation.walkthrough: Cos is the standard short form of cosine, and y is a common variable, so cos y reads as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means snug and warm, and split differently it is the cosine function applied to y.

clue.text: Journalist died, Times agree, in early spring?

indicators.note: what is in something sits inside it

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season falling in early spring
ob. abbreviates obiit, Latin for died
by means times, as in three by four
to correspond is to agree or match

explanation.surface: A reporter dies, and the newspaper confirms it happened early in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign; Lent's period from Ash Wednesday to Easter wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby correspondent is a political reporter accredited to Parliament, briefed privately by ministers and officials.

clue.text: Greeting famous person, receiving answer, extremely short

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece holds others

parts.note: a name is a celebrity, as in a big name
A is the abbreviation for answer

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of short

explanation.surface: A celebrity gives a very brief hello after being asked a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely short' gives just the two end letters, which join the answer letter inside the celebrity before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Namaste is a respectful Hindu salutation spoken with palms pressed together, a form of saying hello.

clue.text: Venture money to win unknown plant

parts.note: to bet on a horse is to stake money on it winning
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes cash on an obscure horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be an agent, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Betony is a purple-flowered herb of the mint family, once used in folk medicine.

clue.text: Most tedious journey, in a way

indicators.note: what is in something sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a ride is a journey
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone describes the most boring trip, in one sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' reads as somewhat; it splits into the insertion signal, A and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid writing or talk is dry and dull, so the superlative means the dullest of all.

clue.text: Incompetent teacher has mislaid book supplement

indicators.note: something mislaid has been lost, so it is no longer there

parts.note: bad means incompetent
a don is a university teacher
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A hopeless lecturer has lost the extra volume he was meant to bring.
explanation.walkthrough: BAD DON loses its first B.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra item attached to something, a supplementary component.

clue.text: After meal, perform music, not serious

parts.note: in Britain tea can be an evening meal
to sing is to perform music

explanation.surface: After dinner, the guests play some light-hearted tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: In much of Britain tea is the early evening meal, not just a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing remarks are playful and joking, said in fun rather than meant earnestly.

clue.text: Achieve much travel with reduced ticket price

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, losing its last letter

parts.note: to go is to travel
a fare is the price of a ticket

explanation.surface: An advert for a bargain fare tells customers they can get a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much travel' tempts as one phrase, but 'Achieve much' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To go far is an idiom for being highly successful, as in that youngster will go far.

clue.text: Wizard goes on curious search

indicators.note: going on something means following after it

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious
a mage is a wizard

explanation.surface: A sorcerer sets off on a strange quest.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for strange, as in a rum do.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to hunt through things untidily, looking for something hidden among them.

clue.text: Holder of secure government post abroad

definitions.text: Holder of secure government post abroad

parts.words: Holder of secure government post abroad
parts.note: surface reading: an official with a safe job at an overseas embassy
setter's reading: post is mail, and the holder is the container that carries it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holder of a post' suggests a person in a job; here post means mail and the holder is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Embassy correspondence travels in sealed pouches that customs may not open under international law.

clue.text: Lear's companion offered to drink last of strong mineral

parts.note: the Fool accompanies King Lear in Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: goods sold have been put up and taken, offered for sale

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of strong

explanation.surface: King Lear's jester accepts a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fool is Lear's truth-telling jester; G goes into SOLD after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron pyrites glitters like the precious metal and has fooled many prospectors, hence its nickname.

clue.text: Indicate approval, having cleaned out dirty seabird

parts.note: a nod signals agreement

indicators.note: something cleaned out is emptied of its contents, keeping just its edges

parts.note: the first and last letters of dirty

explanation.surface: Someone gives a nod of approval once a filthy gull has been washed.
explanation.walkthrough: Noddy is also a children's toy character, but here it is the tropical tern.
explanation.definitionFit: The noddy is a dark tropical tern, named for its nodding courtship display, a type of ocean bird.

clue.text: In barrel, see brewing gallons — of these?

definitions.text: In barrel, see brewing gallons — of these?

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients and transforms them into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Look into the cask and you will see gallons of something brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition: what might be brewing by the gallon in a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagers are beers brewed in large vats and stored in casks, so they fit the scene described.

clue.text: Like some kings to take power ahead of time

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Certain monarchs seize control before they are due to.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London costermongers who wear suits covered in pearl buttons for charity events.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearly king is a Cockney charity figure in a button-studded costume, not a real monarch.
